title: matchCounts are mis-attributed to wrong breakpoint rows when boundaries are out of order or contain blank/invalid rows
description: BreakpointGrid renders `matchCounts[i]` against breakpoint row `i` in the array's original order, but the caller (BandingEditor) computes matchCounts from `breakpointsToRules(...)`, which SORTS boundaries ascending and FILTERS out blank/non-numeric rows (and may append an extra open-ended band). The two arrays therefore do not align index-for-index whenever the user's breakpoints are not already in strict ascending numeric order, or contain a blank/invalid intermediate row. The displayed per-band match count is then attached to the wrong band, silently giving the user incorrect feedback while editing.
evidence: BreakpointGrid.tsx:251-254 renders `{matchCounts[i] ?? "—"}` keyed by row index `i` (rows are shown in raw `breakpoints` order, never sorted). In BandingEditor.tsx:149-159, for `banding === "breakpoints"`: `const contRules = breakpointsToRules(bpRules, factor.rightClosed ?? true); return contRules.map(cont => previewRows.filter(...).length)`. bandingUtils.ts:233-296 `breakpointsToRules` does `bounded.sort((a,b) => a.boundary - b.boundary)` (line 252) and skips blanks/NaN (lines 243-249), producing rules in sorted, filtered order plus an optional appended open-ended rule (lines 287-293). Trace: breakpoints rows [{boundary:"30",label:"High"},{boundary:"10",label:"Low"}] -> contRules[0]=`<=10` (Low band), contRules[1]=`10<x<=30` (High band) -> matchCounts=[count(<=10), count(10..30)]. Grid row 0 ("High") shows matchCounts[0] = the Low-band count (wrong); row 1 ("Low") shows the High-band count (wrong). With a blank intermediate row [{"10","Low"},{"",""},{"20","Mid"}], contRules has length 2 so grid row 2 ("Mid") reads matchCounts[2]=undefined -> "—", and blank row 1 reads matchCounts[1]=Mid's count. The existing test (BreakpointGrid.test.tsx:291-306) only uses already-sorted numeric rows so it passes despite the gap.
